title: Custodian · timeline
alt: Word, mouth and gaze timing for each voiced cue
credit: Newly written interpretive narration for this visit, spoken by a synthetic voice (gpt-4o-mini-tts, onyx). Not a historical quotation unless the cue names its manuscript.

title: Custodian · greeting
alt: Good afternoon, and welcome to Travellers Rest. I am John Overton, or the likeness Ralph Earl painted of me in 1817. This is my library. The books beside my quills are the Tennessee Reports. A descendant of mine, another John, keeps his own work in the cabinet by the window. Where shall we begin?
credit: Newly written interpretive narration for this visit, spoken by a synthetic voice (gpt-4o-mini-tts, onyx). Not a historical quotation unless the cue names its manuscript.

title: Custodian · projects
alt: Then come to the cabinet by the south window. It belongs to John, my descendant. Each volume on its shelves is one of his projects. Choose a spine, and it will come to your hands.
credit: Newly written interpretive narration for this visit, spoken by a synthetic voice (gpt-4o-mini-tts, onyx). Not a historical quotation unless the cue names its manuscript.

title: Custodian · letters
alt: On the writing table lies a letter I wrote to General Jackson on the fifth of November, 1832. Lift it, and read my hand for yourself. Three more of my papers addressed to him are in the chest by the north wall.
credit: Newly written interpretive narration for this visit, spoken by a synthetic voice (gpt-4o-mini-tts, onyx). Not a historical quotation unless the cue names its manuscript.

title: Custodian · room
alt: You are standing in the southwest room of the house I began in 1799. The federal survey of 1970 marks it Library. By 1808 I kept about one hundred and sixty law books here. Others lived and laboured on this land, and the house book on the table tells their part of the story.
credit: Newly written interpretive narration for this visit, spoken by a synthetic voice (gpt-4o-mini-tts, onyx). Not a historical quotation unless the cue names its manuscript.

title: Custodian · explore
alt: Then the room is yours. Touch whatever interests you. I shall be here above the mantel if you want me.
credit: Newly written interpretive narration for this visit, spoken by a synthetic voice (gpt-4o-mini-tts, onyx). Not a historical quotation unless the cue names its manuscript.

title: Custodian · bookmark
alt: Welcome back. Your place is marked. Shall I have the book brought to you?
credit: Newly written interpretive narration for this visit, spoken by a synthetic voice (gpt-4o-mini-tts, onyx). Not a historical quotation unless the cue names its manuscript.

title: Custodian · cabinet
alt: I will leave you with John's present-day work. The screen in his cabinet shows it running.
credit: Newly written interpretive narration for this visit, spoken by a synthetic voice (gpt-4o-mini-tts, onyx). Not a historical quotation unless the cue names its manuscript.

title: Custodian · project-generic
alt: A good choice. I shall leave you to read it.
credit: Newly written interpretive narration for this visit, spoken by a synthetic voice (gpt-4o-mini-tts, onyx). Not a historical quotation unless the cue names its manuscript.

title: Custodian · book-companion
alt: The house book is a visitor's companion. Its four leaves tell of the land before the house, of the household, of a campaign, and of the law reports.
credit: Newly written interpretive narration for this visit, spoken by a synthetic voice (gpt-4o-mini-tts, onyx). Not a historical quotation unless the cue names its manuscript.

title: Custodian · object-overton-letter
alt: This is the letter itself. I sent Jackson a speech of Mr. Poinsett's, and I wrote: No man living but yourself can bring to a calm the perturbed spirits of the Southerners, respecting this unfortunate Tariff. Every page of the scan is here, with a transcription beside it.
credit: Newly written interpretive narration for this visit, spoken by a synthetic voice (gpt-4o-mini-tts, onyx). Not a historical quotation unless the cue names its manuscript.

title: Custodian · object-william-franklin
